inputs.label: The poster
inputs.note: The artwork as supplied. It is used as both the first and the last frame, so the clip loops and the typography cannot drift.

params.prompt:
Warm evening light, shallow depth of field, unhurried.

Timeline:
[0s-2s] The sign fills the frame, light catching its edge.
[2s-5s] Slow drift back, the street coming into view behind it.

No cuts, no camera shake, no text overlays.

Audio: Low room tone, distant traffic, no music.

values.value:
Animate the source artwork as a motion poster, preserving its exact layout, palette, typography and composition. [describe the artwork here: its border, colours, style, main subject]

It is one continuous, unbroken, locked-off take that holds on this artwork for the entire duration — a single shot, no cuts, staying on the poster from the first frame to the last.

Everything in the artwork that could move, moves. Find the photographed subjects — people, faces, food, drink, fire, water, foliage, fabric, lights, machinery — and animate each one continuously and clearly throughout the clip, with the motion that thing really has: people breathe, blink and shift their weight, liquid swirls and settles, flames flicker and throw light, foliage stirs, reflections and highlights travel across surfaces. The movement should be plainly visible, not subtle — the poster is a live scene, not a still.

The text and logos hold their designed positions throughout. The camera is locked off and the final frame returns to the original artwork.
